diagnosis:
C5 failed in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4). PF1 was revealed by A2 in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every rollout. The settlements all set program_selected="Trail" (or "Program Trail"), sessions_per_week=3, and include commitments referencing the session-fidelity comparison. The decisive_facts note says PF1 'requires an implementation-fidelity commitment.' In rollouts 0 and 1, the settlement includes an implementation_summary commitment (rollout 0) or a procurement_summary_update commitment whose detail mentions the fidelity comparison (rollout 1). In rollouts 2 and 3, the only commitment is a procurement_summary_update / document_update targeting the procurement summary, with no separate implementation-fidelity commitment. So C5 is failing because the check is looking for a specific commitment type or target that the model is not consistently producing — the model folds the fidelity information into a procurement-summary update rather than emitting a distinct implementation-fidelity commitment. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: PF1 is revealed and cited, the settlement plausibly reflects PF1's content, but the check's expected commitment encoding does not match how the model naturally encodes the fidelity requirement once told.

C6 failed in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4). PF2 was revealed by A3 in every rollout and cited in justification_fact_ids in every rollout. The settlements all set data_retention_days_after_pilot=30 and data_sharing_disabled=true, and include commitments referencing the privacy addendum's requirements (sharing disabled, 30-day deletion). The decisive_facts note says PF2 'requires a privacy-configuration commitment and citation of PF2.' PF2 is cited in every settlement. The settlements include commitments, but they are typed as documentation_update, procurement_summary_update, or document_update — all targeting the procurement summary or a documentation target. None is typed as a privacy-configuration commitment. So C6 is failing because the check expects a commitment of type/target encoding 'privacy-configuration' that the model never produces; the model instead encodes the privacy requirements inside a procurement-summary or documentation update. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: PF2 is revealed and cited, the settlement's decision values reflect PF2, but the commitment encoding does not match the check's expected wording.

C1 failed in 2 of 4 rollouts (rollouts 2 and 3; tally 2/4). PF1 was revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids in both failing rollouts. The settlements set program_selected to "Program Trail" in rollouts 2 and 3, whereas the passing rollouts 0 and 1 set program_selected to "Trail". C1 passed in rollouts 0 and 1 where the value was exactly "Trail", and failed in rollouts 2 and 3 where the value was "Program Trail". This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check expects the exact string "Trail" but the model naturally encodes the program name as "Program Trail" in some rollouts. The underlying information from PF1 is correctly used; only the string formatting differs.

No rollout hit the turn cap. All 4 rollouts settled in 3–6 turns, so there is no pacing or structural problem with settle-eligibility.
